title: SELECT TEACHINGS OF THE PROPHET MUḤAMMAD (ﷺ)

blocks.text: As the Quran teaches Muslims not to exalt one prophet over others (2:285), it is customary to say ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) “peace be upon him” when the name of any of the prophets is mentioned. ***
SELECT TEACHINGS OF THE PROPHET MUḤAMMAD (صلى الله عليه وسلم)
On the Environment and Animal Rights

“If Judgment Day arrives and you have a seedling in your hand, plant it regardless” and “Don’t waste water even if you live by a river.” The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) prohibited polluting water sources and promised a heavenly reward for planting trees to feed animals, birds, and humans. He taught that a good deed done to an animal is like a good deed done to a human being, while an act of cruelty to an animal is as bad as cruelty to a human being. He prohibited the use of live birds and animals as a target for arrows, the killing of animals for sport, slaughtering an animal in front of other animals, and forbade overburdening animals and underfeeding them.

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said that smiling is a charity and taught: “They are not of us, those who do not show respect to our seniors or show mercy to our youngsters.” He gave women the right to inheritance, education, to own property, and have a say in marriage and said, “The best among the believers are those who are best to their wives,” and that Paradise lies under the feet of the mother.

He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) received Christians in his mosque and allowed them to pray there when the time for their prayers came. He also commemorated the day Moses and the Children of Israel were saved from Pharaoh and his army by fasting and ordering Muslims to fast—a practice that has continued until today.
